title: Lists, Tuples, Sets, Dicts
goal: List, tuple, set aur dict mein data rakhna, badalna, dhundhna aur ginna seekhoge; list of dicts ko mini dataset ki tarah filter/group karoge, comprehensions likhoge, aur samjhoge ki kaunsa dibba kab aur kyun fast hai.

lessons.title: List — ek dibba, kai cheezein
blocks: Ab tak ek variable mein **ek value** thi. Lekin GEEP ke 50 cable products ka naam rakhna ho to 50 variables banaoge? Nahi. Iske liye **list** hai.
**List** = items ka **ordered collection**. Ordered matlab jis order mein daala, usi order mein rehta hai. Square bracket `[ ]` aur items ke beech comma.
List ek train jaisi hai: har dibba (item) ka ek number hai, aur dibbe line mein jude hain. Naya dibba peeche jod sakte ho, beech se nikaal bhi sakte ho.

cables = ["5 Core", "3 Core", "Fiber", "XLPE"]
print(cables[0])
print(cables[-1])
print(len(cables))
Index **0 se** shuru hota hai. Negative index peeche se ginta hai: `-1` = aakhri, `-2` = second last. Kyun 0 se? Kyunki index ka matlab hai "shuru se kitna door"; pehla item 0 door hai.
**Slicing** = list ka ek tukda. `list[start:stop]` — start shamil, stop **shamil nahi**.
Dhyan se dekh: `nums[1:3]` mein index 1 aur 2 aaye, 3 nahi. `[::-1]` = poori list ulti. IQ mein yeh trick bahut poochte hain.
**Mutable** = badal sakti hai. String mein `s[0] = "x"` error deta tha, list mein chalta hai.

cables = ["5 Core", "3 Core", "Fiber"]
cables[1] = "4 Core"
cables.append("PVC")
cables.insert(0, "2 Core")
print(cables)
cables.remove("Fiber")
last = cables.pop()
print(last)
print(cables)

['2 Core', '5 Core', '4 Core', 'Fiber', 'PVC']
PVC
['2 Core', '5 Core', '4 Core']
`pop()` / `pop(i)` = index se hatao aur item wapas do

a = [1, 2]
a.append([3, 4])
print(a)
b = [1, 2]
b.extend([3, 4])
print(b)
Common galti (IQ trap): `append([3, 4])` poori list ko **ek item** bana deta hai. Alag-alag jodna ho to `extend`.

nums = [5, 1, 4, 1]
print(nums.count(1), nums.index(4), 4 in nums)
new = sorted(nums)
print(new, nums)
x = nums.sort()
print(x, nums)
Common galti: `x = nums.sort()` likha to `x` mein **None** aayega. `.sort()` original list ko hi badal deta hai aur kuch return nahi karta. Nayi list chahiye to `sorted(nums)`.

prices = [100, 250, 400]
for i, p in enumerate(prices):
    print(i, p)
print("Total:", sum(prices))

a = [1, 2, 3]
b = a
b.append(4)
print(a)
c = a.copy()
c.append(99)
print(a, c)
`b = a` naya dibba nahi banata, sirf **same list ka doosra naam** rakhta hai (jaise ek ghar ke do address). Asli copy: `a.copy()`, `a[:]` ya `list(a)`.

lessons.title: Tuple aur Set — fix data aur unique data
blocks: **Tuple** = list jaisa ordered collection, lekin **immutable** — ek baar bana, phir badal nahi sakta. Gol bracket `( )`.
Tuple = pakki likhi hui marksheet. Padh sakte ho, lekin number badal nahi sakte. List = pencil se likha rough page.

10
Error: 'tuple' object does not support item assignment

**Kyun chahiye?** Jo data badalna hi nahi chahiye (GPS coordinates, RGB color, database ki ek row, config) use tuple mein rakho. Galti se badlega hi nahi. Tuple thoda **fast** aur kam memory wala bhi hai, aur **dict ki key** ban sakta hai (list nahi ban sakti).
Common galti: ek item ka tuple banana ho to **comma zaroori** hai: `(5,)`. Sirf `(5)` to bas number 5 hai.
**Unpacking** = tuple ki values seedha alag variables mein. Yeh Python mein har jagah dikhega, ML code mein bhi (`X_train, X_test = ...`).

point = (10, 20)
x, y = point
print(x, y)
a, b = 1, 2
a, b = b, a
print(a, b)

def min_max(nums):
    return min(nums), max(nums)

low, high = min_max([4, 9, 2])
print(low, high)
Function jab `return a, b` karta hai to asal mein ek **tuple** return hota hai, aur hum use unpack kar lete hain. Swap `a, b = b, a` bhi tuple unpacking hi hai.
**Set** = sirf **unique** items ka collection, **koi order nahi**. Curly bracket `{ }`. Duplicates khud hat jaate hain.

codes = [101, 102, 101, 103, 102]
unique = set(codes)
print(unique)
print(len(unique))
unique.add(104)
unique.discard(101)
print(sorted(unique))
Set ke maths wale kaam — "kaunse customers ne dono mahine order kiya?" jaise sawal ek line mein:
Dhyan se dekh: maine set ko `sorted()` karke print kiya. Set ka order fix nahi hota, isliye text wale set ka print order har baar alag aa sakta hai.
Common galti: `x = {}` **khali set nahi**, khali **dict** hai. Khali set: `set()`. Aur set mein index nahi hota: `s[0]` error dega.
**Where (ML mein):** ek column ki unique categories nikalna (`set(cities)`), duplicate rows hataana, do datasets ke common IDs dhundhna, vocabulary banana (unique words).

lessons.title: Dictionary — naam se value dhundho
blocks: List mein index se dhundhte ho: `cables[47]`. Lekin yaad kaise rakhoge ki 47 pe kya hai? **Dictionary** mein **naam (key)** se dhundhte ho.
Phone ki contact list: "Anna" search karo, number mil gaya. Yeh yaad nahi rakhna ki Anna contact number 47 pe hai. Ya GEEP ka item code: code bolo, poori cable ki detail mil jaaye.
**Dictionary (dict)** = `key: value` pairs ka collection. Keys **unique** hoti hain. Python 3.7+ mein dict insertion order yaad rakhta hai.

cable = {
    "name": "5 Core Cable",
    "size": "16 sqmm",
    "price": 4500,
    "in_stock": True
}
print(cable["name"])
print(cable["price"])
print(len(cable))
**CRUD** = Create, Read, Update, Delete. Dict mein chaaron ek-ek line ke hain:

user = {"name": "Akash", "age": 25, "city": "Bhiwadi"}
user["email"] = "a@x.com"   # naya key = add
user["age"] = 26            # purana key = update
del user["city"]            # delete
removed = user.pop("email")
print(user)
print(removed)
Jo key hai hi nahi, use `[ ]` se maangoge to **KeyError** aur program crash. Safe tareeka `.get()`:

user = {"name": "Akash"}
print(user.get("phone"))
print(user.get("phone", "N/A"))
print("name" in user, "phone" in user)
Real code mein, jahan key ho bhi sakti hai aur nahi bhi (jaise API ka JSON), `.get(key, default)` use karo. `in` sirf **keys** check karta hai, values nahi.

name
price
stock
name: 5 Core
price: 4500
stock: 12
['5 Core', 4500, 12]
`.keys()` = sirf keys, `.values()` = sirf values, `.items()` = dono (key, value) tuple ban ke.
**IQ ka sabse famous sawal: counting.** "Har word kitni baar aaya?" — NLP aur ML mein yahi pehla step hota hai (word frequency).

from collections import Counter
c = Counter("cable pass cable fail cable pass".split())
print(c.most_common(2))
Common galti: dict ki key **mutable nahi** ho sakti. `{[1, 2]: "x"}` TypeError (unhashable type: list) dega. Key ke liye str, int ya tuple use karo.

lessons.title: Nested data aur comprehensions — mini dataset
blocks: Real duniya ka data (API, database, CSV) aksar **list of dicts** ban ke aata hai. Har dict = ek **row**, har key = ek **column**. Yahi ek mini dataset hai — aage Pandas DataFrame bhi isi tarah socha jaata hai.
Dhyan se dekh: `leads[0]` = pehli row (dict), phir `["name"]` = us row ka column. Bahar se andar ki taraf padho.
**Group by** — har city ka total amount. Pandas ka `groupby` bhi andar yahi karta hai:

leads = [
    {"name": "Rahul", "city": "Delhi", "amount": 50000},
    {"name": "Neha", "city": "Jaipur", "amount": 20000},
    {"name": "Amit", "city": "Delhi", "amount": 35000},
]
total_by_city = {}
for lead in leads:
    city = lead["city"]
    total_by_city[city] = total_by_city.get(city, 0) + lead["amount"]
print(total_by_city)
biggest = max(leads, key=lambda l: l["amount"])
print(biggest["name"])
by_amount = sorted(leads, key=lambda l: l["amount"], reverse=True)
print([l["name"] for l in by_amount])
`key=lambda l: l["amount"]` ka matlab: "har row ko uske amount se compare karo". `lambda` ek chhota bina-naam ka function hai (Stage 3 yaad kar).
**List comprehension** = loop + append ko ek line mein likhna. Padho aise: "**yeh do**, **har x ke liye** jo list mein hai, **agar** condition sahi ho".

squares = []
for x in range(5):
    squares.append(x * x)
print(squares)

squares = [x * x for x in range(5)]
print(squares)
evens = [x for x in range(10) if x % 2 == 0]
print(evens)
labels = ["PASS" if v >= 500 else "FAIL" for v in [520, 480, 610]]
print(labels)
**Dict comprehension** aur **set comprehension** bhi hote hain:
**ML se connection:** model ko numbers chahiye. List of dicts se ek column nikaalna ya features ki list banana — sab comprehension se hota hai:

rows = [
    {"size": 16, "cores": 5, "price": 4500},
    {"size": 10, "cores": 3, "price": 2600},
]
X = [[r["size"], r["cores"]] for r in rows]
y = [r["price"] for r in rows]
print(X)
print(y)
Common galti: bahut lambi, 3-3 `for` wali comprehension mat likho. Padhne mein mushkil ho jaaye to normal `for` loop hi behtar hai. Code insaan ke liye bhi likhte hain.

lessons.title: Sahi dibba chuno + Big-O ki samajh
blocks: Chaaron dibbe ka farak ek table mein (book se):

blocks.title: List vs Tuple vs Set vs Dict
head: Order
Duplicate
Change

blocks: Items ki line chahiye, order zaroori → **List**
Duplicates hatane hain, ya tez 'hai ya nahi' check → **Set**
Data fix rehna chahiye, ya dict key chahiye → **Tuple**
Ab ek gehri baat jo IQ mein poochi jaati hai: **list mein dhundhna slow kyun, aur set/dict mein fast kyun?**

List = bina register wali dukaan. "5 Core cable hai?" — dukaandaar ek-ek shelf dekhega. 10 lakh items ho to 10 lakh shelf. Set/Dict = register wali dukaan: code dekha, seedha shelf number pata, ek second mein jawab.

**Big-O** batata hai ki data badhne pe kaam kitna badhta hai. List mein `x in list` = **O(n)** (n items to n tak check). Set/dict mein `x in set` = average **O(1)** (constant), kyunki woh **hashing** use karte hain: key se ek number (hash) banta hai jo seedha uski jagah batata hai.

blocks.title: Lookup ka kaam vs data size

blocks: Upar chart mein points = list (seedhi line upar jaati hai, O(n)); flat line = set/dict (O(1)).

Same value ka hash hamesha same hota hai, isliye set/dict seedha us jagah pe pahunch jaate hain. Isi wajah se **key immutable** honi chahiye — badal gayi to hash badal jaayega aur dict use dhundh hi nahi paayega.

import time
big_list = list(range(1_000_000))
big_set = set(big_list)
t = time.perf_counter(); _ = 999_999 in big_list; t_list = time.perf_counter() - t
t = time.perf_counter(); _ = 999_999 in big_set; t_set = time.perf_counter() - t
print(f"list: {t_list:.6f}s, set: {t_set:.6f}s")
Isse chalao to list wala time set se **hazaaron guna zyada** aayega (exact number har machine pe alag hota hai, isliye output yahan nahi likha).

Real tip: agar loop ke andar baar-baar `if x in badi_list` likh rahe ho, to pehle `badi_set = set(badi_list)` bana lo. Code turant tez ho jaayega. IQ mein yeh optimization bolna bahut impress karta hai.

blocked = ["u7", "u9", "u3"]
users = ["u1", "u3", "u5", "u9"]
blocked_set = set(blocked)
allowed = [u for u in users if u not in blocked_set]
print(allowed)

Common galti: set ka order maan ke chalna. Order chahiye to list rakho ya `sorted(set)` karo. Aur `list(set(nums))` duplicates to hata dega, lekin order bigad sakta hai; order bachana ho to `list(dict.fromkeys(nums))`.

teach.say: Socho 50 cables ke naam rakhne hain. 50 variables? Nahi. Ek list banao — ek train jisme har dibba ek item.
Index zero se shuru. Minus one matlab aakhri. Aur slicing mein stop wala index shamil nahi hota.
List badal sakti hai: append end mein jodta hai, pop end se nikaalta hai. Lekin dhyan: b = a copy nahi, same list ka doosra naam hai.
teach.code:
b = a        # same list
c = a.copy() # asli copy

teach.say: Tuple list jaisa hai par pakka likha hua — badal nahi sakte. Fix data ke liye, aur unpacking mein bahut kaam aata hai.
Set sirf unique cheezein rakhta hai. Duplicate apne aap gayab. Aur common nikaalna ho to and wala nishaan.
Dictionary mein index nahi, naam se dhundhte hain. Key bolo, value lo. Bilkul phone contact jaisa.
Counting ka pattern yaad kar lo: abhi tak ki ginti do, nahi hai to zero, phir plus one. IQ mein pakka aata hai.
Real data list of dicts hota hai: har dict ek row, har key ek column. Yahi tumhara pehla mini dataset hai.
Comprehension matlab loop aur append ek line mein: yeh do, har x ke liye, agar condition sahi ho.
teach.code: [x * x for x in nums if x > 0]

teach.say: Aakhri baat: list mein dhundhna ek-ek shelf dekhna hai, O(n). Set aur dict register jaisa hai, seedha jagah pe, O(1). Badi list mein baar-baar dhundhna ho to set banao.

quiz.why: Start index 1 shamil, stop index 3 shamil nahi: index 1 aur 2 = [20, 30].

quiz.q: `a = [1, 2]; b = a; b.append(3); print(a)` ka output?
quiz.why: `b = a` copy nahi banata; dono same list ko point karte hain, isliye a bhi badal gayi.

quiz.q: `x = nums.sort()` ke baad `x` mein kya hoga?
quiz.why: `.sort()` list ko in-place badalta hai aur None return karta hai. Nayi list ke liye `sorted()`.

quiz.q: Ek item ka tuple kaise banega?
quiz.why: Comma se tuple banta hai; `(5)` sirf number 5 hai.
Khali curly brackets = dict. Khali set ke liye `set()`.
`&` intersection hai: dono mein common items.

quiz.q: Dict mein missing key safe tareeke se kaise padhenge?
quiz.why: `.get()` key na ho to error ki jagah None ya diya hua default deta hai.

quiz.q: Inme se kaunsa dict ki key **nahi** ban sakta?
quiz.why: List mutable hai, isliye unhashable; dict key immutable (hashable) honi chahiye.

quiz.q: `[x * 2 for x in range(4) if x % 2 == 1]` ka result?
10 lakh IDs mein baar-baar 'yeh ID hai ya nahi' check karna hai. Sabse tez kya?
quiz.why: Set hashing use karta hai: membership check average O(1), list mein O(n).

iq.q: List aur tuple mein kya farak hai? Kab kya use karoge?
iq.a: List mutable hai (badal sakte ho), tuple immutable. Tuple thoda fast aur kam memory wala hai, aur hashable hone ki wajah se dict key ya set item ban sakta hai. Badalne wala data list mein (products ki list), fix data tuple mein (coordinates, DB row, function se multiple return values).

iq.q: Python list, set aur dict mein lookup ki time complexity kya hai aur kyun?
iq.a: `x in list` O(n) hai kyunki ek-ek item check hota hai. Set aur dict hash table pe bane hain, isliye `x in set` aur `d[key]` average O(1) hain: key ka hash seedha uski jagah batata hai. Worst case (bahut collisions) O(n) ho sakta hai, par practically rare hai.

iq.q: append aur extend mein kya farak hai?
iq.a: `append(x)` x ko ek single item ki tarah end mein jodta hai, chahe x list hi kyun na ho: `[1,2].append([3,4])` → `[1, 2, [3, 4]]`. `extend(iterable)` har item alag-alag jodta hai → `[1, 2, 3, 4]`.

`list.sort()` original list ko in-place sort karta hai aur None return karta hai; sirf list pe chalta hai. `sorted(iterable)` nayi sorted list return karta hai, original same rehti hai, aur kisi bhi iterable (tuple, set, dict keys) pe chalta hai. Dono `key=` aur `reverse=` lete hain.

iq.q: Shallow copy aur deep copy kya hai?
iq.a: `b = a` copy hi nahi, same object ka naya naam hai. `a.copy()` ya `a[:]` shallow copy hai: bahar ki list nayi, lekin andar ki nested lists same objects. `copy.deepcopy(a)` andar tak sab naya banata hai. Nested data (list of lists/dicts) mein deepcopy chahiye taaki original na badle.

iq.q: Dict ki key mutable kyun nahi ho sakti?
iq.a: Dict key ka hash nikaal ke value ki jagah tay karta hai. Agar key badal jaaye to hash badal jaayega aur dict use dhundh nahi paayega. Isliye key hashable (immutable) honi chahiye: str, int, float, tuple (agar andar bhi immutable ho). List ya dict key dene pe `TypeError: unhashable type`.

iq.q: List se duplicates kaise hataoge, order bachate hue?
iq.a: Order zaroori nahi: `list(set(nums))`. Order bachana ho: `list(dict.fromkeys(nums))`, kyunki dict insertion order yaad rakhta hai aur keys unique hoti hain. Ya ek `seen` set ke saath loop chala ke.

iq.q: String mein har character/word ki frequency kaise nikaaloge?
iq.a: Dict ke saath: `for w in words: count[w] = count.get(w, 0) + 1`. Ya `collections.Counter(words)`, jo `most_common(n)` bhi deta hai. Yeh NLP mein bag-of-words aur vocabulary banane ka base hai.

iq.q: List comprehension kya hai, aur kab use nahi karni chahiye?
iq.a: Ek line mein loop + optional filter se nayi list banana: `[x*x for x in nums if x > 0]`. Normal loop + append se short aur thoda fast hai. Lekin jab logic complex ho, nested loops 2 se zyada hon, ya side effects (print, file write) hon, tab normal loop zyada readable hai.

iq.q: Generator expression aur list comprehension mein kya farak hai?
iq.a: `[x*x for x in nums]` poori list memory mein turant banata hai. `(x*x for x in nums)` generator hai jo ek-ek value maangne pe banata hai, isliye badi data pe memory bachta hai. `sum(x*x for x in nums)` jaisa likhna common hai. Generator sirf ek baar iterate hota hai.

iq.q: ML mein raw data ko list of dicts se features (X) aur labels (y) mein kaise badaloge?
iq.a: Har row dict hai, to comprehension se: `X = [[r["size"], r["cores"]] for r in rows]` aur `y = [r["price"] for r in rows]`. X ek 2D list (rows x features) ban jaata hai jo baad mein NumPy array ya Pandas DataFrame mein jaata hai. Missing values ke liye `r.get("size", 0)` jaisa default.
